items.title: Loretta Rowland Evans Interview
items.q: I used to rush and see the king come in by the river... we'd be right by the river banks to see the king come in.

ctx.x: Do you remember when the Zulu Parade used to start or didn't it used to start on Bayou St. John?

Uh, the Zulu Parade, I used to go see it. I used to remember when it used to come up the river on a Bayou and they'd get off the float. They'd get off the boat and then have a bunch of the maids waiting for them and the Zulos with the grass, guys dressed just like Zulos and they'd all be jigging and waiting, dancing and there would be a van waiting on the shore for them and they'd all march off. But it was, it was so much nicer and also during Carnival, a long time ago, the Monday of Carnival, I had what you call…
He's got one on Howard Avenue now, but you mean this was on a boat? Came in on a boat. The Zulu came in by Janky's. It's way downtown.
